headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 9 studies yielded an effect size of 1.22 (95% CI: 0.99–1.51), indicating no statistically significant association between zinc and prostate cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 63.72%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
